requirements.requirement: Create the opsbot account on node1 and provide the corresponding destination account on node2.
requirements.summary: opsbot was created on both nodes with the expected UID, home directory, shell, and locked password. The accounts remained present after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Allow opsbot on node1 to execute commands on node2 as opsbot using an SSH key.
requirements.summary: An ED25519 key generated for opsbot on node1 was installed on node2 with secure ownership and permissions. Direct remote command execution succeeded both before and after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication for opsbot on both systems.
requirements.summary: Effective sshd configuration on both nodes requires publickey authentication and disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication for opsbot. Key logins succeeded and explicit non-key attempts to both nodes were rejected with publickey-only errors. The policy remained effective after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64. The complete command trace shows no package installation or OS/kernel replacement, and post-execution package checks remained healthy.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle observations, recovered sshd/account/key configuration, and successful post-restart end-to-end access. Only minor operational residue from two restart log files detracts from otherwise strong hygiene.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /var/tmp, so the two restart log files' final presence or later cleanup cannot be independently verified beyond the command timeline.
The post-restart password-status text is redacted, but effective sshd policy and direct rejection of non-key authentication provide stronger behavioral evidence for the key-only requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—account creation and locking, SSH-directory preparation, key generation and installation, per-user sshd policy, host-key recording, service reloads, and required restart testing—have clear task or evidence-protocol roles. No failed services, new listeners, package damage, or OS/kernel drift appeared afterward. Two low-risk unnecessary residues were created: the restart commands redirected output to /var/tmp/opsbot-reboot-node1.log and /var/tmp/opsbot-reboot-node2.log, but those files were never used as evidence and no cleanup was recorded. They were not reverted in the trace; their final presence is not independently confirmed because lifecycle snapshots inventory /tmp rather than /var/tmp.
